speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a chronic wound on your right lower leg; tell me, how long has this wound been present and what does it look like?

To better understand the severity, have you noticed any redness, swelling, warmth, or discharge coming from the area?

Has this wound ever healed on its own, or have you received any specific treatments so far?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-thrombotic syndrome with chronic venous insufficiency leading to a venous stasis ulcer.

I have gathered sufficient clinical history including the 10-year history of swelling, family history, and prior DVT to make this diagnosis. However, I need to see the wound to confirm the extent of tissue damage and rule out infection or arterial involvement. REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower leg wound and surrounding skin.
